blocks.text: Lots and land in Burnaby Lake

items.t: Lot character: typical lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only sourced size figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds in (280 m² / 281 m²), which are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

The park is not land supply: Burnaby Lake Regional Park is 360 acres, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978 under a 25-year lease agreement with the City signed February 2025; the lake and park lands are park and conservation land, not housing land, and a home here does not come with lake frontage rights.

Serviced position: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a garbage toter fee, with the detached single-family water charge at $652.33 and sewer for single-family homes billed as a sewer parcel tax — the established streets sit inside that municipal system on the City's wording; servicing for any single parcel is confirmed with the City, not confirmed parcel-by-parcel here.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Burnaby Lake is confirmed; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission. No ALR percentage split is stated.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Burnaby Lake

items.t: Burnaby Lake is a City of Burnaby GVR board sub-area wrapping Burnaby Lake Regional Park in central-east Burnaby — residential streets on the lake's edges (Sperling/Kensington west and north-west, Government Road/Beaverbrook east) around a large regional park and lake that are not themselves residential land. Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park; "Burnaby Lake" the sub-area is the housing around it.
Nearby areas: Montecito and Sperling-Duthie north and west, Government Road east, Burnaby Hospital and Deer Lake south-west, Lougheed Town Centre further east along Lougheed Highway.

Main roads: Lougheed Highway (north), Winston Street, Sperling Avenue, Kensington Avenue and Government Road; Highway 1 runs along the lake's south side. Transit: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, walkable into the park, with bus routes 110, 134 and 144 connecting there; route 110 runs past the lake's north and west sides between Lougheed Station and Metrotown Station. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.
Nearest hospital: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, immediately south-west.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) — 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide, no middle-school tier (K–7 / 8–12). SD41 schools beside the sub-area on the Province's list: Sperling Elementary (K–7), 2200 Sperling Ave; École Seaforth Elementary (K–7), 7881 Government Rd; Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Burnaby Lake

items.t: Lake-edge diligence: the lake shore is low, marshy wildlife habitat; a floodplain designation for the sub-area's residential streets was not confirmed in the sources read. For lake-edge and creek-edge lots, check flood, habitat and watercourse-setback conditions early — setback surprises surface late in deals.

Bare-land strata rules (applies to any bare-land strata lot, if one is ever verified here): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Burnaby Lake ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burnaby Lake

items.t: The park's management is locked in for a generation (Feb 5, 2025): the City and Metro Vancouver signed a 25-year lease for Burnaby Lake Regional Park; Metro Vancouver continues to fund maintenance, natural resource protection, enforcement and capital improvements, and will develop a Park Management Plan with the City within five years — the green edge beside these lots is not a future development phase.

Two lakes' names are used interchangeably on Canada Way: Savile Row is filed under Burnaby Lake and marketed as the "heart of Deer Lake" — a buyer searching only one lake's name will miss or double-count product around the south edge.

The sports complex is the west side's real amenity engine: 5 lit artificial turf fields, 17 tennis courts in the City's listings, and the 2,000-seat Bill Copeland rink — with programs continuing during construction of the new recreation centre, so the amenity story carries a construction period with it.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot on Burnaby Lake?
faq.a: No verified one — the lake itself is a 360-acre regional park, and the surrounding streets are built fee-simple house lots. No bare-land subdivision or presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: Does a park-edge home come with lake frontage or dock rights?
faq.a: No — the park is public land managed by Metro Vancouver under a 25-year agreement; a home borders or overlooks the park, it does not come with lake frontage rights, and the park's wildlife rules are part of living there.

faq.q: How many units can a house lot here hold?
faq.a: Under the R1 SSMUH rules: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop — Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station proximity is the parcel-specific question on the west side. Confirm the parcel's district and transit distance with the City.

faq.q: What checks does a lake-edge lot need?
faq.a: Flood, habitat and watercourse-setback checks, early — the shoreline is protected wildlife habitat, and no floodplain designation for the residential streets was confirmed, so the position is parcel-specific.

faq.q: Is Burnaby Lake a neighbourhood or a park?
faq.a: Both names are in use for different things: Burnaby Lake Regional Park is a 360-acre Metro Vancouver regional park around the lake, managed by Metro Vancouver since 1978 under a 25-year lease agreement with the City, and "Burnaby Lake" is also the GVR MLS® sub-area name for the housing on the streets around it.

faq.q: What can you do at Burnaby Lake?
faq.a: Metro Vancouver describes a wildlife sanctuary with walking trails, viewing towers and docks, a Nature House, and a rowing course with a pavilion and public canoe launch at the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex; the complex itself has 5 lit artificial turf fields and 17 tennis courts in the City's listings.

faq.q: How is transit at Burnaby Lake?
faq.a: Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) sits at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway at the area's north-west side, you can walk into the park directly from the station, and buses 110, 134 and 144 connect there — the 144 links the station to Metrotown and SFU.
